Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X67/X67n1301.xml). Chan Master Foguo's Record of Struck Measures on the old cases. Yuanwu Keqin owns the retained deployment: on the raised eleventh case of Qinshan raising his fist - open it is a palm, five fingers uneven; closed it is a fist, no high or low - when a monk comes out of the crowd and raises his own fist, Yuanwu's interspersed verdict strikes: is there no end to fellows playing with mud balls? Qinshan's answer that the monk is merely a no-opening-no-closing fellow also earns thirty blows, and Xuedou's pick follows.

Jingyin Facheng, the Cheng Kumu of Xiangshan in Ruzhou, owns the exact utterance preserved in the imperial anthology's life of Hongzhi Zhengjue: when the young Hongzhi first gained an insight on hearing the Lotus Sutra and presented a drawn circle thrown behind him in the master's room, Xiangshan rules - is there no end to fellows playing with mud balls? - and sends him to find someone else; Hongzhi answers wrong and is sent on to Danxia.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB464.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qizong Zhen of Huayan. Yaoshan Weiyan owns the exact utterance inside Qizong Zhen's raising: asked on the level plain with shallow grass how to shoot the chief among the herd, he says watch the arrow; the monk throws himself down as if shot, he calls the attendant to drag out this corpse, the monk runs, and he rules - is there no end to fellows playing with mud balls? Qizong Zhen appraises that though it looks like acting on the cue, it still dodges blade and avoids sword; able to win taking the point head-on, truly a battle-tested officer.

Senses.Explanation: Yaoshan dismisses the unnamed questioner's staged collapse and escape as one more mud-ball performance, asking how such performers could ever run out. Yaoshan Weiyan uses the expression through complete active quotation of Yaoshan's deer-shooting exchange followed by direct appraisal. Hanyue Fazang independently deploys it through independent deployment of the verdict against the wind-banner explanation.
